question: How can transcendent bliss be both the root of nectar and bliss born of non-bliss?
premises: Transcendent bliss is a sole root of nectar.
Bliss can be described as born of non-bliss.
This paradox is a great mystery.
inference: Supreme bliss transcends ordinary oppositions, appearing even through what seems unlike bliss.
uncertainties: The paradoxical phrase na-ānanda-ja-ānanda admits multiple doctrinal interpretations.
plain_english: O sole root of the nectar of transcendent bliss, O bliss born of non-bliss, O great mystery.
